sdk_integration_plan.already_implemented_rule: Add the missing public SDK contract/adapter/proof to the existing owner backlog; preserve validated core evidence and reuse its implementation.
sdk_integration_plan.not_yet_implemented_rule: Deliver shared Rust service and SDK adapter/proof together inside the same canonical L3/L2 milestone owner; do not defer SDK to a separate delivery track.

settings_parts_2026_10_27.next_action: Open the OpenMatrix9 window and run each Builder icon: preview, change one option, Enter to commit and Cancel, then sign the M06-UI review for each L3.
limitations: 4 Prongs Close builds the sheet's closer pair: both North-side prongs sit inside the 4 Prongs 0 spacing and stay two distinct prongs.
A selection without gem objects is refused: the builder consumes the shared gem row instead of guessing.
A tight row can put the facing prongs of two stones on one point; the builder merges that pair into one shared prong and reports merged_prongs rather than refusing the style.
Border=On consumes the last committed channel border; the app never re-derives a border from the row.
Corner smoothing is the documented 0..1 angle; the exact Matrix corner radius law is not verified.
Count and Spacing are alternatives: setting one clears the other, and the last bead sits on the end fraction.
Curve mode needs a curve: it follows the picked curve, or the committed channel border with Border=On; with neither it is a typed Missing('metal piece curve'), never a row-offset body.
Cutter features are committed as bodies but never weighed; the report counts them under excluded_cutters.
Drop is negative-up per the sheet wording; the UI still has to confirm the sign on the preview.
F4 direction falls back to world +Z at the world centre.
Only a selected circle rail is accepted; an arc or line rail returns a typed refusal.
SettingsMass is a text command without a toolbar slot; mass covers settings features committed in this session.
The base bead diameter is 1.0 mm (OM9 engineering default); the sheet only gives the scale.
The editor rebuilds from the om9.settings.prong payload; a body without it is refused rather than re-derived.
These are command options, not a toolbar icon; the record says so instead of inventing an icon id.

head_bezel_2026_10_27.next_action: Open the OpenMatrix9 window and run Head Builder (basket and half bezel), the four edit levels, the three Bezel Builder modes and the Scallop Bezel: preview, change one option, Enter to commit, Cancel, then sign the M06-UI review for each L3.
limitations: A field outside the level's scope is refused as invalid head edit level field instead of being silently widened.
A payload without the om9.settings.head slot is refused rather than re-derived.
A scallop cutter is the edge profile extruded along the outline tangent; the cut itself is not performed here (the scallop is a separate cutter body).
A selection without a gem object is refused: the builder consumes the gem owner's om9.gem record.
Boolean=On is evaluated in the section frame: the finger rail is a ring on the same girdle, so the groove is the rail section swept along the outline. A non-ring target would need the 3-D CSG owner.
Cutter bodies never weigh in the metal mass; the report adds their cutter volume and the net metal (a bound on the removed metal) so the numbers are not silently ignored.
Half-bezel mode ignores the prong profile (the manual states there are no prong profile options in half-bezel mode) and reports it as prong_profile_ignored.
Level 1/2/3 edit the whole prong or rail set; only Level 4 with Prong=/Rail= edits a single element.
Profile=Bezier:x,y;x,y;... samples a closed cubic Bezier into a typed section; Profiles never insert a scene object, they only shape a builder section.
Prong clearance is measured against the inscribed girdle radius; a faceted outline is inscribed in its profile circle.
The band follows the girdle arc between Position and Position+Span; the white rotation handle is UI scope.
The committed Finger Rail body is an Insert alongside the notched ring; it carries the same om9.settings.bezel payload so a rebuild can find it.
The default head drop follows the stone (35% of the pavilion depth, capped at 0.9 mm) so the base stays above the culet.
The edge profile drives the corner shape only; the section parameters (height/top/base/dome/angle/chamfer) are explicit typed values.
The library is read-only built-ins plus the session's user list; ProfileSave= keeps a user section and Profile=<name> resolves it. The Bezier control-point editing UI is not part of this owner.
The seat cutter is a trapezoid wedge under the girdle; the cut is a mesh CSG difference and refuses a non-closed result.
The seat frames are published here; Enter applies the seat cut to the gem body through Mutation::Geometry on the gem owner's entity, so Undo restores both the stone and the head.
Under Bezel shifts the section below the girdle band; Gallery Rail is one ring below it. Both share the closed-ring and Boolean gates.
Validity is measured per body (closed, positive volume, unique ids) on the generated mesh; the OCCT B-Rep swap is the kernel adapter's own gate.
